clues: This small town sits on steep bluffs by a great river. It looks out on the wide water from the east bank.
Winters here are long, dry, and cold, and summers are hot. Spring and fall hurry past in brief swings.
Founded in 1880 on the river, this town was selected as the state capital when its state joined the Union in 1889. Rival towns fought hard for the honor.
Just one state capital in the land has fewer folks than this small town. Yet it holds the top job for the whole wide state.
The governor of South Dakota works in this city. Lawmakers travel here from across the wide plains to make the state's laws.
